text: Good morning, Pip! It's a perfect day!
Look what Gran Mari gave me! A job!
I get to look after this seed!
It looks like a tiny rock.
But it's not a rock. It's a seed!
What does a seed need?
Let's find out!
Where should the seed go?
The dark shelf! It's closest. Quick, quick!
Ollie, you didn't ask anyone!
Oops. I rushed again. What do you think, Bean?
Great idea, Bean! It's warm and bright here.
Job done! The seed is on the sill. Time to play!
Doesn't a seed need more than a sill?
I've got a faster way! Seeds grow all by themselves.
I'll check on it later. Much later!
What if we try the careful way? Let's ask Gran Mari.
Okay. We'll check on the seed tomorrow.
Today the seed grows! I bet it's huge!
It didn't change at all!
Is it a tree yet? I did not forget!
Gus, did you give it anything to drink?
Drink? Um. Yes! Lots. It drank it all. Very fast.
But the jar is dry, Gus.
That's just its dry look! Very fashionable!
Seeds like it warm! I'll hatch it!
Whoa! I'm fine! I meant to do that!
Gus, what does a seed really need?
I don't know. Seeds are small. How hard can it be?
We need help. Let's ask Gran Mari.
Well now, a yarny seagull and a puzzled otter. What's all this?
Gran Mari, what does a seed need?
Oh, that is a good question, Ollie. Let's find out together.
I set these up last week. Same seeds, same sunny window.
Only one thing is different. The towel.
That looks just like our seed.
This one is waking up!
Water wakes a seed up. A warm spot helps too. Then the green shoot reaches for the light.
It's growing toward the sun!
Well now, what do you think happens next?
The seed wakes up! But not right away.
Right. A seed takes time. It can't be hurried.
Try it at home! Ask a grown-up to help you.
Wet a paper towel and fold it. Put it in a clear bag with a bean.
Tape the bag to a sunny window. Check it every day.
I have to say something. I fibbed.
I said it drank lots. It didn't. I forgot all about it.
Thanks for telling us, Gus.
One shell for every day I check. That's my job.
Water!
You're right, Bean! I almost forgot again!
It's growing! It's really growing!
Look! A tiny green hat on a seed!
Time for my Wonder Pocket! Three things we learned.
One. A seed needs water to wake up.
Two. A warm, sunny spot helps it grow.
Three. A seed needs time. We can't hurry it.
And one kind thing to try today. Look after something small. Give it water!
Bye, everybody! I'm off to water my seed!
